subject: armadillo
pitch: A nine-banded armadillo trotting along. A shell of overlapping banded plates in dusty pinkish-tan, a pointy snout, tall leathery ears, small beady eyes, sturdy clawed feet and a long armoured tail tapering to a point. A sprinkle of coarse pale hairs pokes out between the bands.
reasoning:
I'm planning out a TypeScript module using the SDK to model a trotting armadillo, using stacked rings or thin cylinder sweeps to build the banded shell, aiming for moderate complexity and realistic proportions based on a nine-banded armadillo's typical body length.

Working out the joint hierarchy next: a root pelvis joint oriented along the forward axis, then chained chest, neck, and head joints each parented to the previous one with aim directions pointing forward, plus a separate tail chain built from a polyline of points trailing behind the pelvis.

Now I'm sketching the four legs as named joint chains per limb, going from shoulder/hip down through knee and ankle to a toe point, parented to the chest or pelvis with matching name arrays per joint.

For the trotting pose, I'm deciding whether to apply rotations to diagonal leg pairs or simply offset the foot positions so front-left and hind-right swing forward together while the opposite pair trails back.

For the body, I'm considering using a loft with stations along z to build a smooth banded shell, then thinking through whether the armadillo's transverse bands can be achieved with striped paint along the z axis so the bands run perpendicular to the spine.

For texture, I'm considering adding fine hair cards between the bands using an SVG texture to give small tufts of pale fur peeking through.

For placement, I'm thinking of generating frames along the body loft surface, computing points and directions on the mesh so hairs orient naturally with weights tied to the nearest joint.

Now I'm shaping the ears as thin extruded slabs — tall leathery outlines positioned symmetrically on either side of the head joint, with specific outline points to give them a pointed, leathery silhouette.

For the head itself, I'm building it from a box for the skull shape plus a cone oriented forward for the pointed snout, using the dir option to aim the cone's axis along the forward direction so the tip juts outward realistically.

Then I'm adding tiny dark spheres for the eyes positioned symmetrically on the front sides of the head, and planning the legs as swept capsule shapes along chains of joints, using b.sweep with a radius and color to generate each leg segment smoothly.

Adding small claws per foot with offset positions, then setting up the tail as a tapered sweep from thick base to thin tip.

For color, I want the tail bands to run perpendicular along its length, so stripes oriented on the z-axis work since the tail extends along -z. I'll reuse the same shell paint pattern for the tail as the body for visual consistency.

For the body, I'm laying out loft stations along z to shape the armadillo's shield-to-body taper, defining width and height at each cross-section from front to back.

I'm binding the loft to a small set of joints—pelvis, chest, neck—so it deforms naturally with the skeleton rather than staying rigid to a single nearest joint, and applying the shell color paint across the whole loft.

For hair, I'm scattering frame-based hair cards along the back using a randomized generator, computing their y-position relative to the body's surface height at each z-station, and leaning them toward a backward flow direction with pale-colored stroke textures rendered as simple curved SVG strands.

Now I'm working out leg chains: four-point polylines for each leg giving three spans and matching joint names (shoulder, knee, ankle, toe), parented to chest or pelvis depending on front or hind position, with toes touching down near y=0 to keep the armadillo low to the ground.

Then I'm defining the spine joint chain -- pelvis, chest, neck, head -- each with position and aim targets so parts attach correctly, followed by a tapered tail chain swept with shrinking radius and rounded-to-pointed end caps for a natural tapering tip.

Now I'm working out leg sweeps and joint positions for a trot pose, placing shoulder, knee, ankle, and toe coordinates for each leg (FL, FR, HL) so the stance looks dynamic with front-forward and back-trailing limb placement, all parented correctly to the pelvis.

For the head, I'm setting up skull geometry as a box parented to the head bone, deciding to keep the shell plates with a plain tan color rather than stripes for simplicity.

Then I'm adding a cone for the snout pointing slightly downward and forward, extruded ear shapes positioned at the top of the head that mirror left and right, sized to look leathery and tall, before moving on to planning the eyes.

Adding small dark spheres for the eyes, then working out the body coloring with a nine-banded stripe pattern using dusty pinkish-tan and darker brown tones, adjusting band spacing to fit across the body length. I'm also darkening the leg color for the belly region and planning to finalize the module by returning the baked root and exporting a build function.

For the hair, I'm figuring out approximate surface heights across the body at different z positions so each hair strand sits just above the shell rather than floating inside it, settling on a roughly constant y value with slight sink for simplicity, and setting the hair direction to point straight up from each frame.

Now I'm working out the card placement — leaning them backward with some spin and size variation using a seeded RNG for determinism, and sketching a loop that scatters hair frames across a z-range with randomized x offsets constrained to stay within the body's width at each slice.

Writing body sweep and tail geometry...

Still defining body part geometry... eyes as small spheres, snout as a tilted cone, and the head as a box positioned and bone-weighted near the top of the skull.
